Title: Fix registry-support renovate

Description:
### Which area is this bug related to?

/area registry


### What versions of software are you using?




### Bug Summary

**Describe the bug:** Konflux Renovate bot seems to be hitting a quota limits for PR changes across patching Konflux tasks and patching the service components.

**To Reproduce:** Scheduled, you can see branches under [devfile/registry-support](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support) that are created by the Konflux Mintmaker Renovate bot that do not have tied PRs and appear incomplete, i.e. [go-deps](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/tree/konflux/mintmaker/main/go-deps) and [major-go-deps](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/tree/konflux/mintmaker/main/major-go-deps).


### Expected Behavior

Renovate config should respect quota limits and setup schedules and groupings that ensure regular patching across the board.

### Any logs, error output, screenshots etc? Provide the devfile that sees this bug, if applicable

The following are incomplete branches from Renovate: 
- [go-deps](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/tree/konflux/mintmaker/main/go-deps)
- [major-go-deps](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/tree/konflux/mintmaker/main/major-go-deps)

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Any workaround?

_No response_

### Suggestion on how to fix the bug

Following changes should be made to resolve quota limits and maximize essential patching on a regular basis:
- Create groupings for each service component under [devfile/registry-support](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support) rather than one big patching branch
- Create different schedules for all of the patching groups: service component patching groups (different schedule for each group), dockerfile patching group, and Konflux task patching group (should remain the same as before, every Tuesday and Thursday night)
- Pin Go versions - we do not need this as we typically handle this manually on an roughly annual basis, we can open a follow up task to implement further renovate config that handles Go bumps separately
- Set PR limits as we do under [devfile/registry](https://github.com/devfile/registry)

**Describe the bug:**

<!--
    A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
-->

Helm Chart expects `global.ingress.domain` to be set when targeting OpenShift clusters. Anything set under `global.ingress` should only pertain to k8s environments.

**To Reproduce:**

<!--
    Steps to reproduce the behavior.
-->

Just using `helm install devfile-registry deploy/chart/devfile-registry --set global.isOpenShift=true` leads to links pointing to devfile registry server endpoints to be not found, because it will use the [current default value](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/blob/dd51121eae680cd52c72733ef1594719fd6e75f2/deploy/chart/devfile-registry/values.yaml#L19) for `global.ingress.domain`.

Using `helm install devfile-registry deploy/chart/devfile-registry --set global.isOpenShift=true --set global.ingress.domain=<openshift-route-domain>` will fix this behavior for the deployment.

## Expected behavior

<!--
    A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->

According to current [documentation](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/blob/dd51121eae680cd52c72733ef1594719fd6e75f2/deploy/chart/devfile-registry/README.md#installing-the-devfile-registry-on-openshift), should not expect a domain name to be passed, alternatively should be separated from ingress fields, i.e. `global.route.domain`.

## Any logs, error output, screenshots etc? Provide the devfile that sees this bug, if applicable

<!--

    api: please copy the terminal output

    integration-tests: please copy the build log under prow ci result for QE ingetration tests
-->

## Additional context

<!--
    Add any other context about the problem here.
-->

### Any workaround?

<!--
    Describe the workaround if applicable.
-->

Seperate domain setting for OpenShift environments to be under `global.route` rather than `global.ingress`, apply this to Route template and `DEVFILE_REGISTRIES` environment variable under the [registry-viewer deployment spec](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/blob/dd51121eae680cd52c72733ef1594719fd6e75f2/deploy/chart/devfile-registry/templates/deployment.yaml#L141-L149), and under [documentation](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/tree/main/deploy/chart/devfile-registry#installing-the-devfile-registry-on-openshift) to describe this.

### Suggestion on how to fix the bug

<!--
    Provide suggestion on how to fix the bug upon your investigation, if applicable.
-->

Ideally, the domain for OpenShift environments should be fetched on deployment to best suite current [documentation](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/blob/dd51121eae680cd52c72733ef1594719fd6e75f2/deploy/chart/devfile-registry/README.md#installing-the-devfile-registry-on-openshift) and sync with [registry-operator](https://github.com/devfile/registry-operator). However, the workaround approach could be used if technical limitations of the helm chart prevents this solution from working.

Title: Registry check with odo v3 fails for outerloop stacks

Description:
## Which area this feature is related to?

/kind bug

### Which area this bug is related to?

/area ci
/area registry
/area test-automation

## Bug Summary

**Describe the bug:**

As seen in a [PR](https://github.com/devfile/registry/pull/226) and [PR](https://github.com/devfile/registry/pull/220) opened by renovate bot, when a stack using additional resources (e.g `Dockerfile`, `deploy.yaml`) the `validate-stacks: check with odo v3` job is failing.

**To Reproduce:**

[On your local environment]

* Go to the `tests/odov3` directory.

* Create a var called stackDirs having the 4 go stack versions as example.
```bash
stackDirs="go/1.0.2 go/1.1.0 go/2.0.0 go/2.1.0"
```

* Create a var called currentPath
```bash
currentPath="$(pwd)"
```

* Create a var called stacks path pointing to the stacks dir
```bash
stacksPath="$(pwd)/../../stacks"
```

* Run the ginkgo command which is used by the `tests/check_odov3.sh`
```bash
ginkgo run --procs 2 -v -trace --slow-spec-threshold 120s   --timeout 2h   $currentPath -- -stacksPath $stacksPath -stackDirs "$stackDirs"
```

## Expected behavior

All tests should be passing. Example:
```bash
=============================================================================
Random Seed: 1697317896

Will run 4 of 4 specs
••••

Ran 4 of 4 Specs in 95.700 seconds
SUCCESS! -- 4 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 0 Skipped
--- PASS: TestOdo (95.71s)
PASS

Ginkgo ran 1 suite in 1m36.77173346s
Test Suite Passed
```

## Any logs, error output, screenshots etc? Provide the devfile that sees this bug, if applicable

The following PRs are related to stack version that support outerloop and as a result require extra resources.

`go/2.1.0`: [PR#226](https://github.com/devfile/registry/actions/runs/6481736291/job/17674532152?pr=226#step:9:144)
`python/3.0.0`: [PR#220](https://github.com/devfile/registry/actions/runs/6458966453/job/17533781444?pr=220#step:9:143)

## Additional context

The reason that this is happening is that the `odo_test.go` is using:
```golang
_, _, err := runOdo("init", "--devfile-path", stack.path, "--starter", starterProject.Name, "--name", starterProject.Name)
```

This command will not copy the `docker/Dockerfile` or the `kubernetes/deploy.yaml` that the `go/2.1.0` contains. So when we try to run `odo dev` the command fails.

### Any workaround?

We could try to copy any additional resources inside the stack dir. 

### Suggestion on how to fix the bug

After this code:
```golang
_, _, err := runOdo("init", "--devfile-path", stack.path, ...
```
We can have a function that will try to copy any files found and don't exist in the destination dir.

## Bug Summary

**Describe the bug:**

<!--
    A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
-->
The `Validate stacks` github action for [the registry repo](https://github.com/devfile/registry) will trigger on every open PR. It will find the change delta and only run the test suite against changed stacks.

However, if the stack contains multiple versions (ie. has a `stack.yaml` in the stack root) and the directory's version name has been changed, the delta will not be correctly picked up.

The delta is created with `get_stacks.sh` and will use a git diff to find the files changed. In the case where an existing version directory name is changed, the diff will look like this:

```
...
stacks/go/{1.0.2 => 1.1.0}/devfile.yaml           | 25 ++++++++++++++++++++++++-
stacks/go/{2.0.0 => 2.1.0}/devfile.yaml           | 25 ++++++++++++++++++++++++-
...
```

and the existing regex (`stacks\/(.*)\/devfile\.yaml`) won't match correctly.

**To Reproduce:**

<!--
    Steps to reproduce the behavior.
-->

Change a version directory in an existing multi version stack and open a PR to trigger the test.

## Expected behavior

The changed version stack should be picked up in the `get_stacks.sh`

## Additional context

<!--
    Add any other context about the problem here.
-->

### Any workaround?

<!--
    Describe the workaround if applicable.
-->

Force `TEST_DELTA` to be false to turn off delta testing.

### Suggestion on how to fix the bug

<!--
    Provide suggestion on how to fix the bug upon your investigation, if applicable.
-->

Update the way `changed_stacks` are found in `get_stacks.sh`

## Bug Summary

**Describe the bug:**

While working on adding support for `autoBuild`  and `deployByDefault` in `odo` (https://github.com/redhat-developer/odo/issues/5694), I needed to handle the case where those fields are not explicitly set in the Devfile and the components are not referenced by any `apply` commands (see https://github.com/devfile/api/issues/852#issuecomment-1211928487).
But currently, the parser automatically sets unset fields to their default values (`false` here) when called with the option to flatten the Devfile:

https://github.com/devfile/library/blob/bd4a12f272573de1ab254f3e138a9b55904af620/pkg/devfile/parser/parse.go#L147-L153

On the other hand, parsing without flattening makes our tests using child and parent Devfiles fail (mainly because the child Devfile was missing other definitions like commands or components - see [the logs here](https://github.com/redhat-developer/odo/actions/runs/4403146219/jobs/7711148764?pr=6654)).

**To Reproduce:**
See this sample project that highlights the issue: https://github.com/rm3l/bug-devfile-parser-fields-not-set

## Expected behavior

As discussed during the community call (on March 20, 2023), flattening should not dictate whether default values should be set or not. It should be up to the clients of the library to decide how to handle unset fields. This is especially necessary since fields like `autoBuild` and `deployByDefault` have 3 states (`true`, `false`, and `nil`) with different behaviors that need to be implemented client-side.

package main

	if err != nil {

odo init --name test-nodejs --devfile nodejs --starter nodejs-starter

PR https://github.com/devfile/api/pull/702 changed how endpoints are validated, forbidding endpoints that use the same port within the same container. Some containers define multiple endpoints to isolate routes. For example, Eclipse Theia requires multiple routes on the same port:

They both have different containerd dependency and hence the collision in containerd function signature. I have not found a workaround using replace directive, will continue working with Dev Console team to see if we have a temporary workaround, but the best solution moving forward is that both helm project and devfile project move forward on Dev Console with the same version or at least backward compatible versions of oras.land/oras-go. Notice that there is already a 1.0.0 version there: https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/releases/tag/v1.0.0. HELM 3.7.1 is currently at 0.4.0

**To Reproduce:**
change Dev Console go.mode helm dependency from 3.6.2 to 3.7.1, then do:
go mod tidy
go mode vendor
/build-backend.sh

You will se following error:

`dperaza@dperaza-mac console % ./build-backend.sh
vendor/github.com/deislabs/oras/pkg/oras/push.go:55:31: not enough arguments in call to remotes.PushContent
        have (context.Context, remotes.Pusher, v1.Descriptor, "github.com/containerd/containerd/content".Store, nil, func(images.Handler) images.Handler)
        want (context.Context, remotes.Pusher, v1.Descriptor, "github.com/containerd/containerd/content".Store, *semaphore.Weighted, platforms.MatchComparer, func(images.Handler) images.Handler)`

Both Helm and Devfile depend on compatible versions of oras from the version referenced in Dev Condole go.mod

Change go.mod to use oras.land/oras-go v0.4.0: https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/blob/main/registry-library/go.mod#L7

The API StartProjects git/remotes description states: `The remotes map which should be initialized in the git project. Must have at least one remote configured` implying that we can have more than one remote defined.  While this is true for regular projects, [validation](https://github.com/devfile/api/blob/main/pkg/validation/validation-rule.md) issues an error if there are more than one `remotes` in a starter project.   

**To Reproduce:**
<!--
    Steps to reproduce the behavior.
-->
There are a couple of ways to reproduce this:
1.  Use a main devfile that has a starterProject configured with multiple git/remotes.  

error will be similar to this:

Test_StarterProjects1.yaml : error validating starter projects:
        starterProject defibhmdqs00001 should have one remote only
        starterProject bfmtxtxtumsxswpvjqwhyuvcrzyxocvzurrthjjqtcpj00011 should have one remote only
```

2. Use a main devfile configured with a parent that overrides a starterProject in the parent devfile i.e.

**main devfile:**

```
 starterProjects:
  - git:
      remotes:
        iNj00001: GxyqiGh00002
    name: nodejs-starter
```

**parent devfile:**

```
starterProjects:
  - name: nodejs-starter
    git:
      remotes:
        origin: "https://github.com/odo-devfiles/nodejs-ex.git"
```

error will be similar to this:

```
error validating starter projects:
        starterProject nodejs-starter should have one remote only, imported from id: nodejs, registryURL: https://registry.stage.devfile.io, in parent overrides from main devfile]
```

## Expected behavior
<!--
    A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->

We should have a clear description in the API and docs stating what the expected behaviour is for projects and starterProjects.  Since the objects all resolve to a common `GitLikeProjectSource` type, we are relying on a shared description which is the source of confusion (see related issue: https://github.com/devfile/api/issues/529)

We should update the description to indicate these differences in both the `projects.go` and `zz_generated.parents_overrides.go` files.  Proposed changes are:

`The remotes map which should be initialized in the git project. Projects must have at least one remote configured while StarterProjects can only have at most one remote configured`

## Bug Summary
**Describe the bug:**

given the devfile like this

```yaml
schemaVersion: 2.1.0
metadata:
  name: test

commands:
- id: build
  exec:
    commandLine: "true"
    component: cmp
    group:
      isDefault: true
      kind: build
- id: run
  exec:
    commandLine: "sleep infinity"
    component: cmp
    group:
      isDefault: true
      kind: run
- id: test-apply
  apply:
    component: cmp-apply

components:
- name: cmp-apply
  container:
    image: quay.io/prometheus/busybox:latest
    command:
      - "echo 'preStart'"
- name: cmp
  container:
    image: quay.io/prometheus/busybox:latest

events:
  preStart:
    - test-apply
 ```

`generator.GetContainers` return only `cmp` and `cmp-apply` container.




## Expected behavior
`generator.GetContainers` should return  only `cmp` container.

Devfile spec says: 

> when an apply command is bound to a preStart event, and references a container component, it will start the container as a K8S initContainer, unless the component has its dedicatedPod field set to true.
> 
> When no apply command exist for a given component, it is assumed the component will be applied at devworkspace start by default.


It is impossible to filter out initContainers from `GetContainers`  output because when calling `GetInitContainers` containers have autogenerated names that don't match containers from `GetInitContainers`

Title: The `links` field in the registry index schema is an incorrect type

Description:
Looking over the [schema for the registry index.json file](https://github.com/devfile/registry-support/blob/master/index/generator/schema/schema.go), I see that the type for the `links` field in the index.json is a custom struct:
```
// Schema is the index file schema
type Schema struct {
	...
	Links           Links    `yaml:"links,omitempty" json:"links,omitempty"`
        ...
}

type Links struct {
	Self string `yaml:"self,omitempty" json:"self,omitempty"`
}
```

However, the type of `links` should just be `map[string]string`, as any field in `links` is considered valid, e.g.:
```
[
  {
    "name": "java-maven",
    "displayName": "Maven Java",
    "description": "Upstream Maven and OpenJDK 11",
    "tags": [
      "Java",

    "language": "java",
    "links": {
      "self": "/devfiles/java-maven/devfile.yaml",
       "vsix": "/devfiles/java-maven/some-plugin.vsix",

    }
  }
]
```
